chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Munqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i the judge. He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him):
What is asceticism in this world? He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has defined that in His Book, and He said:
So that you may not grieve at the things that pass you by, nor rejoice over that which has been given to you.

key_terms.الدنيا: This world, worldly life (as opposed to the hereafter)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of asceticism (zuhd) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), when asked by the judge Hafs ibn Ghiyath about the definition of zuhd (asceticism/detachment from worldly life), directed him to the Quran rather than offering a personal definition. He cited verse 57:23, which teaches that true asceticism means being emotionally detached from worldly gains and losses -- neither grieving over what is missed nor rejoicing excessively over what is obtained. This response was given in Medina during the Imam's teaching circles, where scholars and jurists like Hafs would come to learn.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Al-Qasim b. Muhammad al-Isfahani narrated to us from Sulayman b. Dawud al-Munqari from Hafs b. Ghiyath al-Nakha`i al-Qadi. He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as):
What is asceticism in this world? So, he said: Allah has defined that in His Book. He says, “
So that you may not grieve at the things you fail to get, nor rejoice over that which has been given to you.” [57:23]
